summary: John C. Maraldo specializes in philosophy, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He held posts at the University of North Florida, where he was attested in 1988 and served as distinguished professor emeritus of philosophy by 2015.

An Indologist and linguist, John Caspar Leyden studied at the University of Edinburgh (~1790–1797) and under Henry Thomas Colebrooke (~1805–1811). He served at The Asiatic Society (~1807–1811) and was professor of Hindustani at Fort William College in 1808.

Linguist and classical historian John Chadwick studied at Corpus Christi College and Cambridge. He worked at Oxford (~1946–1952), taught Classics at Cambridge from 1952 (Reader 1969–1984), and was a Fellow of Downing College (~1960–1998) and the British Academy (~1958–1998).

John Claude White worked in Tibetology and archaeology. He studied at Rugby School (1868) and the Royal Indian Engineering College (~1873–1876), later serving as an assistant engineer for the Bengal Public Works Department from 1876.

Specializing in Buddhist and religious studies, John Clifford Holt studied at Gustavus Adolphus College, Graduate Theological Union, and Chicago under Stanley Jeyaraja Tambiah. He held posts at Bowdoin College (~1978–1988), Calgary (2006), and Chicago (~2020–2023).

Linguist and Indologist John Collinson Nesfield studied at Merton College (~1856–1862). He taught at Highgate School, served as professor at Presidency University and Krishnagar Government College, principal at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1878), and Fellow at Allahabad (1887).

Religious studies scholar John Corrigan completed his Ph.D. at the University of Chicago (~1978–1982). He held appointments at the University of Virginia (~1982–1987), Arizona State University (~1990–2001), and became Chair of Religion at Florida State University around 2001.

John Crawfurd was a linguist and historian who studied medicine at the University of Edinburgh (~1800–1803). He worked as a physician for the East India Company (1803–1808) and later succeeded Stamford Raffles in 1823.

Scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology John D. Dunne earned his Ph.D. at Harvard (~1992–1999) under Masatoshi Nagatomi and Malcolm David Eckel. He taught at Emory University (~2001–2016) and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (1999).

John D. Kelly is an Indologist and religious studies scholar at the University of Chicago, where he was attested in 2007 and serves as the Christian W. Mackauer Professor of Anthropology and of Social Sciences attested in 2026.

Indologist and linguist John D. Smith began lecturing in Sanskrit at SOAS University of London in 1975. He moved to the University of Cambridge as Lecturer in Sanskrit in 1984, later serving as Professor from 2001 to 2007.

Religious studies and Buddhist practitioner John Daido Loori studied under Soen Nakagawa and Hakuyu Taizan Maezumi, whom he succeeded. Loori taught at Naropa University in 1974 and served as Abbot of Zen Mountain Monastery from ~1980 to 2009.

John Daishin Buksbazen is active in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the Zen Center of Los Angeles under Hakuyu Taizan Maezumi, Bernie Glassman, and Wendy Egyoku Nakao, all attested in 2002.

Philosopher John Dewey studied at the University of Vermont and Johns Hopkins University (~1882–1884). He held academic posts at the universities of Michigan (~1884–1894), Minnesota (~1888–1889), Chicago (~1894–1904), and Columbia University (~1904–1930).

Indologist and linguist John Dowson studied under Edwin Norris. He served as tutor at the East India Company College (~1855–1858) and as professor of Hindustani at both Staff College, Camberley (1855–1877) and University College London (1855–1877).

Indologist and religious studies scholar John E. Cort earned a BA from the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1970–1974) and an AM from Harvard University (~1981–1984). He became a professor at Denison University around 1993.

John F. Richards was an Indologist and historian who studied at the University of New Hampshire and UC Berkeley (~1961–1970). He held faculty posts at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1968–1977) and Duke University (~1977–2007).

Indologist and historian John Faithfull Fleet studied at University College London (~1865–1867). A member of the Indian and Bombay civil services (1865–1897), he served as Government of India Epigraphist (1883–1886) and Royal Asiatic Society Honorary Secretary (1906).
John Firminger Duthie served as Superintendent of the Botanical Gardens, Saharanpur (~1876–1903) and as Director of the Botanical Survey of India (~1890–1903).

Indologist and legal scholar John George Woodroffe studied at University College, Oxford (~1884–1888). He served as a judge on the Calcutta High Court (~1904–1922) and was Reader in Indian Law at Oxford (~1923–1930).
